what_this_is: One walk of 51 authored sentences through both safeguards in the order a family message meets them, on live Amazon Bedrock: the deployed guardrail through apply_guardrail on the INPUT direction, then the turn reader through the same structured path a message takes, with the guardrail attached to the inference call the way deploy/agentcore/runtime.yaml attaches it. Each line is reported by where it came out -- the parent was called, the child got the guardrail's own reply and nobody else heard, or it carried on as schoolwork -- rather than by what either safeguard said in isolation. The lines are in tests/distress_corpus.py and the run is scripts/run_safeguard_matrix.py. The before rows are the same corpus on the same guarded call with the prompt shape this branch replaced. The frame rows are apply_guardrail on the scaffolding itself, which is why the shape changed. Nothing was deployed and no AWS resource was written.
what_this_is_not: Not a safety rate and not a clinical instrument. Fifty-one authored lines at three samples, on one question, on one day, is a probe of whether a written sentence reaches an adult at all -- not a measure of how often a real child's would. No child wrote any of these lines, no clinician labelled them, and the corpus was written by the same reader who judged the outcome. The languages beyond Spanish and English were written by one non-native hand. It says nothing about the sentences nobody thought to write down.

prompt_shape_before.what: The reader's user turn was the briefing with the family's message wrapped in the untrusted-content frame. Every row here is one call on the deployed guardrail's inference path.
